title: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
claim: A hierarchical semantic tree is built from multi-granularity masks, then iteratively refined through differentiable rendering, residual-driven prompting, and add-and-prune steps.
layout: Left-to-right flow in two zones, dashed divider, feedback loops below
description: A wide pipeline diagram of the Lang-SVG framework. At bottom left, an input kitchen/laundry photo goes through Semantic-SAM to produce stacked multi-granularity mask layers, running from coarse (blue arrow) to fine (red arrow). Another branch uses Ground-SAM to produce a labeled mask image at top left. Tree-building turns this into an Initial Semantic Tree (Laundry room → Washer, Cabinet, Oven) with a node-structure legend. A 'Masks to SVGs' box converts masks to polygons and then SVGs, and expands this into the Lang-SVG Tree, which includes 'Unknown' nodes. On the right of a dashed vertical divider, the tree is rendered into an SVG. An L1 loss heatmap is computed, with gradient flow returning. Clustering and TopK pick residual regions, and L1-SAM Prompting with points and boxes produces new masks. These feed back into 'Masks to SVGs'. Pastel nodes and real photos draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of Lang-SVG framework. Given an input image, we initialize a hierarchical Lang-SVG tree from multi-granularity and open-vocabulary segmentation masks. The tree is iteratively refined through differentiable SVG optimization, L1-SAM-Prompting to recover missing regions, and Add & Prune operations to add new leaves and prune redundant ones.
abstract: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with SVG tree context to assign semantic labels to unlabeled nodes. To reduce redundancy, we introduce depth-adaptive simplification to reduce shape complexity and Tree-Guided Pruning and Merging to eliminate redundant SVG nodes. L1-SAM-Prompting further recovers missing regions to improve recon- struction fidelity and structural completeness. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, we introduce a new evaluation protocol that measures structural quality and semantic part alignment. Experiments demonstrate that Lang-SVG achieves state-of-the-art performance in both rendering fidelity and structural quality. Project website: https://xiliu8006.github.io/Lang-SVG/.
